cliwerk 4.7.7.1 API

cliwerk (a fork of picocli) is a framework for creating Java command line applications with almost zero code.

The project contains multiple modules, but most applications only need a few of them. The table below shows the JPMS module name and the Maven coordinates for all modules in the project.

cliwerk modules: JPMS module name and Maven coordinates
cliwerk module JPMS module name Maven coordinates (without version)
cliwerk (Java package picocli) info.picocli io.github.wstein:cliwerk (also contains the cliwerk-spec classes, package cliwerk.spec, when built with Java 11+)
cliwerk-spec (Java package cliwerk.spec) none (bundled into info.picocli) bundled into io.github.wstein:cliwerk, not published on its own
cliwerk-spec-tool (Java package cliwerk.spec.tool) none not published by cliwerk (fat jar cliwerk-spec-tool-<version>-all.jar via ./gradlew :cliwerk-spec-tool:shadowJar)
picocli-codegen info.picocli.codegen not published by cliwerk (upstream: info.picocli:picocli-codegen)
picocli-groovy info.picocli.groovy not published by cliwerk (upstream: info.picocli:picocli-groovy)
picocli-shell-jline2 info.picocli.shell.jline2 not published by cliwerk (upstream: info.picocli:picocli-shell-jline2)
picocli-shell-jline3 info.picocli.shell.jline3 not published by cliwerk (upstream: info.picocli:picocli-shell-jline3)
picocli-spring-boot-starter info.picocli.spring.boot not published by cliwerk (upstream: info.picocli:picocli-spring-boot-starter)

Most applications will only need the main cliwerk module (Java package picocli), but we recommend also configuring the picocli-codegen module as an annotation processor for your project. This provides compile-time error checking and generates GraalVM configuration files under META-INF/native-image/picocli-generated/$project during compilation, to be included in the application jar. This in turn facilitates converting your command line application to a native image.

The picocli-groovy module allows Groovy scripts to use picocli annotations for even more compact code.

The picocli-shell-jline2 and picocli-shell-jline3 modules are of interest to applications that want to provide an interactive shell-like console.

The picocli-spring-boot-starter module provides Spring integration. Particularly, it allows for @Autowired or @javax.inject-annotated program elements in picocli components (commands, subcommands, type converters, default providers, etc.) to be injected with values from Spring's Application Context.
